Common correlated effects for panels with unobserved common factors

Source: R/dpnl.R
ccepnl.Rd

The common correlated effects estimators of Pesaran (2006) for a panel whose errors hold unobserved common factors with unit-specific loadings, correlated with the regressors: the dependent variable and the regressors averaged across units in each period (with the weights w) are added to each unit's regression, with the observed common factors d_t (a constant, with cons = TRUE, and the columns of fac). With H = (D, ybar_w, Xbar_w) and M = I - H (H'H)^- H' (eq 15, a generalized inverse), the unit estimates are b_i = (X_i'M X_i)^-1 X_i'M y_i. The mean group estimator CCEMG is their mean (eq 53), with the nonparametric variance sum (b_i - b_MG)(b_i - b_MG)' / (N (N - 1)) (eq 58). The pooled estimator CCEP is (sum w_i X_i'M X_i)^-1 sum w_i X_i'M y_i, the pooling weights equal to the averaging weights as Theorem 3 requires, with the variance of eqs 67-69, sum w_i^2 Psi^-1 R Psi^-1, Psi = sum w_i X_i'M X_i / T and R = sum wt_i^2 (X_i'M X_i / T) (b_i - b_MG)(b_i - b_MG)' (X_i'M X_i / T) / (N - 1), wt_i = w_i / sqrt(mean(w^2)). Inference is normal.

Usage

ccepnl(
  y,
  x,
  unit,
  time,
  fac = NULL,
  cons = TRUE,
  w = NULL,
  avg = NULL,
  level = 0.95
)

# S3 method for class 'ccepnl'
plot(x, ..., main = NULL, col = NULL, pal = NULL)

Arguments

y

The outcome of each row: finite numbers.

x

The regressors: a numeric matrix or data frame, one row per row of y. For plot(), a ccepnl result.

unit

The unit of each row: labels.

time

The period of each row: numbers; each unit at most once per period.

fac

NULL or observed common factors: a numeric matrix or data frame, one row per row of y, constant within each period.

cons

TRUE (default) for a constant among the observed factors, unit-specific intercepts.

w

NULL (equal weights 1 / N, as Pesaran 2006, sec. 5.2, says is typical) or a positive weight of each row, constant within each unit; they are scaled to sum to 1 over the units.

avg

NULL (default: the averages of y and of every column of x, Pesaran's choice) or the averages kept among the columns of H: "y" and names of columns of x.

level

The confidence level of the intervals.

...

Passed to the base-graphics call.

main

NULL (a default title) or one string.

col

NULL (the palette) or colours.

pal

NULL (the session palette, see plotopt()) or a palette name for blpal().

Value

An object of class ccepnl, a list: mg and pooled, the CCEMG and CCEP estimates (term, est, se, z, p, lo, hi); bi, the unit estimates (units by regressors); vmg and vp, the variances; fit, one row (units, periods, k, h the columns of H, n the rows); w, the weights by unit; and level.

Details

Pesaran (2006) derives the estimators for a balanced panel. An unbalanced one is handled as standard implementations handle it (Ditzen 2018, p. 586, says only that xtdcce2 "supports unbalanced panels"; Su, Wang and Wang 2026, p. 2, that "calculating cross-sectional averages of the dependent variable and covariates remains straightforward in unbalanced panels"): the averages of a period are taken over the units observed in that period, their weights scaled to sum to 1 over those units, and each unit's regression runs over its own periods, with its rows of H. CCEMG and its variance are then as above. CCEP is (sum w_i X_i'M_i X_i)^-1 sum w_i X_i'M_i y_i, and in its variance each X_i'M_i X_i is divided by the unit's own number of periods, which is this function's reading of T there. On a balanced panel all of this is Pesaran's estimator. Su, Wang and Wang (2026, p. 2) caution that when whether a unit is observed is related to the regressors, the factors or the loadings, the averages no longer proxy the factors well. A period observed for one unit only, or a unit with fewer periods than its regression needs (twice the regressors, the averages kept and the observed factors), is refused by name.

Juodis and Reese (2026, sec. 1) draw two lessons this function leaves to the user: the averages used can bias the estimates and their variance, so results should be checked against the number and kind of averages (avg keeps a subset; lesson 1), and under Pesaran's assumptions a two-way fixed-effects estimator (fepnl()) may still be consistent and is worth comparing (lesson 2). With slopes common to all units and T not small against N, the intervals of CCEP are not centred without a bias correction, which this function does not make (lesson 1, sec. 3.1). For cross-sectional dependence in the residuals see pcdtst().

The plot draws the CCEMG and CCEP estimates of each regressor with their intervals and returns what it drew.

References

Pesaran, M. H. (2006). Estimation and inference in large heterogeneous panels with a multifactor error structure. Econometrica, 74(4), 967-1012. doi:10.1111/j.1468-0262.2006.00692.x

Ditzen, J. (2018). Estimating dynamic common-correlated effects in Stata. The Stata Journal, 18(3), 585-617. doi:10.1177/1536867X1801800306

Su, L., Wang, F. and Wang, Y. (2026). Estimation and inference for unbalanced panel data models with interactive fixed effects. Journal of Econometrics, 255, 106222. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2026.106222

Juodis, A. and Reese, S. (2026). Five lessons for applied researchers from twenty years of common correlated effects estimation. Journal of Econometrics, 253, 106120. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2025.106120

Examples

# 30 provinces over 12 years, one unobserved factor in y and x
set.seed(9)
d <- expand.grid(year = 1:12, prov = paste0("p", 1:30))
f <- rnorm(12)[d$year]
g <- rnorm(30, 1)[as.integer(substring(d$prov, 2))]
d$x <- g * f + rnorm(360)
d$y <- 1 + 0.7 * d$x + g * f + rnorm(360)
r <- ccepnl(d$y, d["x"], d$prov, d$year)
r
#> ccepnl: common correlated effects, 30 units, 12 periods
#> mean group (CCEMG):
#>  term       est         se        z            p        lo        hi
#>     x 0.7534011 0.06556476 11.49095 1.464985e-30 0.6248965 0.8819056
#> pooled (CCEP):
#>  term       est         se        z            p        lo        hi
#>     x 0.7581987 0.06456047 11.74401 7.580526e-32 0.6316625 0.8847349
